# JSON Toolkit — Full Reference for AI Systems

> Complete technical reference for toolgarden.xyz

## Site Structure

Base URL: https://toolgarden.xyz
Supported locales: en (English, default), zh (Chinese Simplified)
URL pattern: /{locale}/{tool-path}
Image tools hub: /{locale}/image
PDF tools hub: /{locale}/pdf
Canonical examples:
- Home: https://toolgarden.xyz/en
- Tool: https://toolgarden.xyz/en/json-format
- Image hub: https://toolgarden.xyz/en/image
- PDF hub: https://toolgarden.xyz/en/pdf

## Tool Reference

### JSON Formatter (/json-format)
- Input: Any JSON or JSON5-like text (unquoted keys, single quotes supported)
- Output: Formatted JSON with 2-space indentation + interactive tree view
- Features: Format, Minify, URL Decode, Unicode Encode/Decode
- Tree view supports: expand/collapse, node copy, node delete, node download
- Auto-formats on input change (300ms debounce)

### JSON Escape (/json-escape)
- Escape: Minifies JSON, then escapes \, ", \n, \r, \t
- Unescape: Reverses the escape operation and pretty-prints

### JSON Repair / Clean (/json-repair)
- Input: JSON-like text with common issues
- Repairs: line/block comments, trailing commas, smart quotes, single-quoted strings, unquoted object keys, True/False/None values
- Output: standard formatted JSON
- Does not use eval; parsing is done through the project JSON utility layer

### JSON Diff (/json-diff)
- Algorithm: Recursive deep comparison by JSON path
- Output: Per-path diff lines with type (added/removed/changed/unchanged)
- Color coding: green=added, red=removed, yellow=changed, gray=unchanged
- Option to hide unchanged lines

### JSON ↔ YAML (/json-yaml)
- Library: yaml@^2.7
- Both directions supported from the same view

### JSON ↔ XML (/json-xml)
- Library: fast-xml-parser@^4.5
- Wraps JSON in <root> element when converting to XML
- Preserves attributes using @_ prefix convention

### JSON → CSV (/json-to-csv)
- Input: JSON array of objects
- Headers: union of all keys across all objects
- Values: properly escaped (RFC 4180)
- Output: downloadable .csv file

### JSON → Excel (/json-to-excel)
- Library: xlsx (SheetJS) @^0.18
- Converts JSON array to Sheet1 of an .xlsx workbook
- Output: downloadable .xlsx file

### Excel → JSON (/excel-to-json)
- Library: xlsx (SheetJS) @^0.18
- Reads first sheet of .xlsx or .xls file
- Supports drag-and-drop upload

### JSON → TypeScript (/json-to-ts)
- Recursively infers types from JSON values
- Generates named interfaces for nested objects
- Detects integer vs float for number types
- Handles arrays, nested objects, string/number/boolean/null

### JSON Flatten / Unflatten (/json-flatten)
- Flatten: converts nested objects and arrays to a flat object with path keys, e.g. `user.roles.0`
- Unflatten: restores nested objects and arrays from path-key objects
- Supports custom delimiters, default `.`

### Image Tools (/image)
- Lists browser-local image editing, compression, conversion, and Base64 image encode/decode tools
- Child tool URLs use the `/image/*` namespace
- Image input data is not uploaded to the server

### Image Compressor (/image/compress)
- Compresses JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, SVG, AVIF, and common browser-decodable images locally in the browser
- Uses Worker + OffscreenCanvas when available, with a Canvas fallback on the main thread
- Preserves the original format by default; an optional WebP mode exports visually safe WebP results
- Tries conservative output candidates and keeps the smallest visually safe result based on pixel-sample comparison
- Keeps the original file when no smaller visually safe candidate is found
- Supports preview comparison, per-file download, and ZIP batch download

### Remove Image Background (/image/remove-bg)
- Removes image backgrounds locally in the browser with @imgly/background-removal and onnxruntime-web
- Loads WASM and ONNX model assets on first use; subsequent uses are usually cached by the browser
- Exports a transparent PNG with the detected foreground
- Shows source and output preview comparison with a checkerboard background for transparency
- Image files are not uploaded to a server

### Image Watermark Remover (/image/remove-watermark)
- Inpaints selected watermark areas locally in the browser with a MI-GAN 512 ONNX Pipeline high-quality model by default, with a LaMa ONNX fallback and fast pixel repair as additional options
- Users drag or resize a rectangular selection over the area to repair
- Supports edge blending to soften the repaired area
- Exports the repaired image as JPG, PNG, or WebP; JPG uses a white background for transparent pixels
- Best suited for images the user owns or has permission to modify, especially plain backgrounds, gradients, screenshots, simple textures, and moderate photo texture repair
- Uses ONNX Runtime Web and browser Canvas APIs, and does not upload image data to a server

### Image Editor (/image/edit)
- Edits JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, SVG, AVIF, and common browser-decodable images locally in the browser
- Uses a Fabric.js canvas so uploaded images can be edited directly without a separate preview pane
- Supports select, brush, marker, rectangle, ellipse, polyline, text, mosaic, blur, eraser, undo, and redo tools
- Rectangle and ellipse tools can draw stroked or filled shapes with selectable colors
- Mosaic and blur create editable region objects; the eraser deletes annotation objects without erasing the original image
- Exports the edited image as JPG, PNG, or WebP; JPG uses a white background for transparent pixels
- Uses browser Canvas APIs and does not upload image data to a server

### Image to JPG (/image/to-jpg)
- Converts PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, SVG, AVIF, and common browser-decodable images to JPG
- Uses a white background for transparent pixels because JPG has no alpha channel
- Supports output quality control, preview comparison, per-file download, and ZIP batch download

### Image to PNG (/image/to-png)
- Converts JPG, WebP, GIF, BMP, SVG, AVIF, and common browser-decodable images to PNG
- Preserves transparency when the browser decoder exposes alpha information
- Supports preview comparison, per-file download, and ZIP batch download

### Image to WebP (/image/to-webp)
- Converts JPG, PNG, GIF, BMP, SVG, AVIF, and common browser-decodable images to WebP
- Supports output quality control, preview comparison, per-file download, and ZIP batch download

### Image to AVIF (/image/to-avif)
- Converts JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, SVG, and common browser-decodable images to AVIF
- Supports output quality control, preview comparison, per-file download, and ZIP batch download
- AVIF encoding depends on browser support; unsupported browsers report an output format error instead of uploading files

### Image to Base64 (/image/to-base64)
- Converts JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, SVG, AVIF, and common browser-decodable images to Base64 Data URLs locally in the browser
- Supports file selection, drag-and-drop image upload, and Ctrl+V clipboard image paste
- Shows the full Data URL and raw Base64 string with copy actions and TXT download
- Reads MIME type, dimensions, and file size locally; image files are not uploaded to a server

### Base64 to Image (/image/base64-to-image)
- Restores `data:image` Data URLs and raw image Base64 strings into Blob-backed image previews locally in the browser
- Detects PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF, BMP, SVG, and AVIF images by MIME type or file signature when possible
- Supports pasted Base64 text, selected `.txt` or `.base64` files, drag-and-drop text files, preview, and image download
- Image content is decoded locally and is not uploaded to a server

### Image Crop (/image/crop)
- Crops JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, SVG, AVIF, and common browser-decodable images locally in the browser
- Supports dragging the crop frame to move it and dragging edges or corners to resize it
- Exports the selected crop area as JPG, PNG, or WebP; JPG uses a white background for transparent pixels
- Uses browser Canvas APIs and does not upload image data to a server

### Image Resize (/image/resize)
- Resizes JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP, SVG, AVIF, and common browser-decodable images locally in the browser
- Keeps the original image aspect ratio by default: entering width calculates height, and entering height calculates width
- Exports the full resized image as JPG, PNG, or WebP; JPG uses a white background for transparent pixels
- Uses browser Canvas APIs and does not upload image data to a server

### PDF Tools (/pdf)
- Lists PDF conversion and page operation tools
- Child tool URLs use the `/pdf/*` namespace
- First release focuses on browser-local PDF conversion and page-level operations
- Includes PDF to Word text extraction for text-based PDFs
- Planned additions include compress, convert to/from images/text/JSON, edit, annotate, sign, watermark, encrypt/decrypt, and OCR

### Convert to PDF (/pdf/to-pdf)
- Converts JPG, PNG, WebP, TXT, Markdown, HTML, EPUB, unencrypted legacy MOBI/PalmDOC, docx, xlsx/xls, and pptx to PDF locally in the browser
- EPUB conversion reads `META-INF/container.xml`, resolves the OPF package document, follows the spine order, extracts XHTML/HTML chapters, and renders the book text into PDF pages
- MOBI conversion supports unencrypted legacy PalmDOC/MOBI text records with no compression or PalmDOC compression
- Encrypted MOBI, AZW/KF8, and complex Kindle files need a future server-side converter such as Calibre
- Word docx conversion extracts document paragraphs from Office OpenXML
- Excel conversion uses SheetJS to extract sheet rows and render tabular text
- PowerPoint pptx conversion extracts slide text from Office OpenXML
- Text, Markdown, HTML, and Office text are rendered through browser Canvas before being embedded into PDF pages so Unicode content can be preserved
- Images are embedded into a PDF page with aspect-ratio preserving scaling
- Uses pdf-lib for PDF generation and fflate for Office OpenXML and EPUB zip extraction
- Legacy doc and ppt files require a future server-side converter such as LibreOffice and are reported as unsupported in the current browser version
- Supports multiple files, per-file PDF download, preview, and ZIP batch download
- Files are not uploaded to a server

### PDF to Word (/pdf/to-word)
- Extracts text from text-based PDF files locally in the browser
- Uses pdfjs-dist for PDF parsing and text extraction
- Generates a downloadable Word DOCX file using Office OpenXML packaging
- Preserves extracted text by page and line for quick editing and copying
- Scanned or image-only PDFs need OCR before they can become editable text
- Complex layout, tables, and image reconstruction are not fully preserved in this first version
- Files are not uploaded to a server

### Merge PDF (/pdf/merge)
- Combines multiple PDF files into a single PDF locally in the browser
- Uses pdf-lib to copy pages from each source PDF into a new document
- Supports drag-and-drop reordering plus move up/down controls
- Shows source page counts and previews the merged result
- Files are not uploaded to a server

### Split PDF (/pdf/split)
- Splits one PDF into multiple documents locally in the browser
- Supports page range groups such as `1-3; 4-6; 7`
- Can also split every page into a separate PDF
- Outputs a ZIP archive containing the split PDFs
- Files are not uploaded to a server

### Extract Pages (/pdf/extract-pages)
- Extracts selected pages from one PDF locally in the browser
- Supports page selections such as `1,3,5-7`
- Outputs one new PDF containing the selected pages
- Files are not uploaded to a server

### Organize PDF (/pdf/organize)
- Reorders, duplicates, and deletes pages from one PDF locally in the browser
- Uses a draggable page list with explicit move, duplicate, and delete controls
- Outputs a new organized PDF and previews it in the browser
- Files are not uploaded to a server

### Subtitle Maker (/subtitle-maker)
- Free online LRC and SRT subtitle editor
- Supports uploading local audio or video for playback preview and timeline calibration
- Supports uploading or pasting SRT / LRC text, parsing into editable subtitle rows
- Lets users edit start time, end time, and subtitle text line by line
- Lets users set the selected subtitle row start or end time from the current media playback position
- Exports edited subtitles as SRT or LRC text files
- Subtitle and media files are processed locally in the browser and are not uploaded to a server

### JSON Schema Generator (/json-schema)
- Output: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12
- Auto-detects formats: date-time, date, email, uri
- Marks all object properties as required
- Handles nested objects and arrays

### JSON Schema Validator (/json-schema-validate)
- Input: JSON data and a JSON Schema object
- Output: valid/invalid state plus error paths and messages
- Supports common JSON Schema keywords: type, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, enum, const, oneOf, anyOf, allOf, min/max string length, regex pattern, numeric bounds, array item bounds, object property bounds, and common formats (email, date, date-time, uri)

### JSONPath Query (/json-path)
- Library: jsonpath-plus@^10.3
- Supports full JSONPath syntax including filters: [?(@.price > 36)]
- Press Enter or click Query button to execute

### JSON Stats (/json-stats)
- Metrics: raw size (bytes), minified size, compression %, max nesting depth, total key count, object count, array count, type distribution, longest string value
- Auto-analyzes on input change (400ms debounce)

### Info Encoder / Decoder (/info-codec)
- Encodes text with legacy Encode (% / %u), Unicode escape sequences, URL percent encoding, UTF16-style \x hex escapes, Base64, hex, and JavaScript string escaping
- Computes MD5 and SHA1 hashes locally in the browser
- Decodes Unicode escape sequences, URL percent encoding, UTF16-style \x hex escapes, Base64, hex, HTML entities, JWT tokens, URL parameters, cookies, gzip payloads, and escaped strings
- URL parameter parsing preserves duplicate keys as arrays
- JWT decoding Base64URL-decodes header and payload without verifying the signature
- Cookie formatting converts semicolon-delimited cookie strings into readable JSON
- Gzip decompression accepts Base64 or hex encoded gzip data
- All operations are implemented in the project utility layer and do not upload input text

### QR Code Generator (/qr-code/generate)
- Generates PNG QR codes from URLs, plain text, contact data, Wi-Fi configuration text, or other strings
- Supports QR size, quiet-zone margin, and error correction level controls
- Uses qrcode@^1.5 for QR generation and outputs a browser-downloadable PNG data URL
- Text input is not uploaded to a server
- Links to QR Code Decoder for the reverse workflow

### QR Code Decoder (/qr-code/decode)
- Decodes uploaded PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF, and BMP images locally in the browser
- Uses Canvas image data and jsQR@^1.4 with inverted-code attempts enabled
- Uploaded images are not uploaded to a server
- Links to QR Code Generator for the reverse workflow

### JWT Parser (/jwt)
- Decode: Base64URL decodes header and payload (no key needed)
- Verify: HMAC-SHA256 via browser Web Crypto API (HS256 only)
- Shows expiry status (expired/valid) if exp claim present
- Includes example token for testing

## Architecture

- Framework: Next.js 16 with App Router
- Language: TypeScript (strict mode)
- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 with semantic design tokens
- i18n: next-intl with [locale] routing
- All tool logic: pure functions in lib/utils/ (no React dependencies)
- Tool registry: lib/tools/registry.ts drives home page and navigation automatically
- SEO metadata: localized canonical URLs, hreflang alternates, WebApplication JSON-LD, ItemList JSON-LD, FAQ JSON-LD, and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD

## Privacy

- Zero server-side processing
- Page-level analytics may be used, but tool inputs are not uploaded
- Locale preference may be stored in a cookie for language routing
- No tool input data is uploaded or stored by the server
- All file operations (Excel, CSV) use browser File API
